pageCache.text:
Departments
Glyne Gap College
Travel Training
Work Placements
The Flat
Working in partnership with the Transitions Team
Seniors
The seniors follow the national curriculum similar to mainstream schools but adapted to suit the learning needs of our pupils. We expect pupils to work hard but equally to have a lot of fun whilst learning. There are 3 classes and most of our formal learning is done in those class groups.
The classes integrate every Tuesday afternoon for sports, leisure and citizenship activities. We encourage all our pupils to be responsible for themselves and their belongings as far as is possible. Our aim is to teach them the skills that will help them cope when they move on to college or other post school provision.

pageCache.pageTitle: Glyne Gap Nursery - our nursery for special needs infants
pageCache.text:
Nursery
Glyne Gap Nursery
CITES for pre-school children
Glyne Gap Nursery
Glyne Gap School offers specialist Nursery provision to children with profound and multiple learning disabilities, and children with complex learning and health needs.
Children do not need an EHCP in place to be part of our Nursery. Nursery places are jointly agreed by the Headteacher and East Sussex County Council SEND Early Years Service. If your child is not known to SEND Early Years Service you can self-refer or ask your child’s nursery or health visitor to refer. Details on how to refer can be found here: SEND Early Years' Service (SEND EYS) | East Sussex 1Space
Please be aware that our Nursery Provision is currently full until September 2027. We are not able to conduct any visits prior to this time. This will be kept under review and the school and Local Authority will continue to work closely to maximise capacity for those children with the greatest needs. If you would like to discuss Nursery provision for September 2027 for your child, or have any concerns about your child's progress and needs, please contact SEND Early Years Service.
Our Nursery is open term time only - Monday to Friday from 09.00am -15.15pm
Early Years Policy (CG11)

pageCache.text:
Departments
Glyne Gap College
Travel Training
Work Placements
The Flat
Working in partnership with the Transitions Team
Infants
Our department consists of 4 classes: Seagulls, Penguins, Wrens and Skylarks - for pupils ranging from 4 - 8 years of age.
When pupils move into infants they are stepping into a new and exciting phase of their educational career.
For the first time they will be attending school full-time, and will meet lots of new experiences and challenges. Building on the skills pupils have already gained in the Nursery, we are committed to seeing pupils learn and make progress towards reaching their full potential in all areas of the curriculum, but particularly in their levels of independence and personal autonomy.
We believe learning should be fun, and endeavour to provide a broad and balanced range of activities and experiences, both in school and within the wider community. Making full use of all the excellent resources we have in school, we teach within our own class groups, but also enjoy regular department activities. Activities to which parents can be invited are regularly planned, as we want parents to feel fully involved in their child's learning.
We have close links with several mainstream schools, and enjoy integrated activities with them. A local secondary school also supports our department and regularly plans special events for the pupils - e.g. summer picnics, Christmas party, etc. We are a busy, hard working, but fun-loving department, and enjoy seeing our pupils learn and grow before handing them onto our colleagues in the Junior department.

Holiday Scheme
We run our own holiday play scheme during most of the school holidays for pupils/students from the age of 4 to 16 years. The day runs from 10.00 a.m. until 4.00 p.m. and costs £25 per day. Days are action packed, using all our indoor and outdoor spaces, and full of fun!

pageCache.pageTitle: Junior education for special needs children
pageCache.text:
Departments
Glyne Gap College
Travel Training
Work Placements
The Flat
Working in partnership with the Transitions Team
Juniors
The Junior department has three classes of Key Stage 2 pupils. In the Juniors pupils build on the skills they have gained in the Infants, particularly in the essential areas of Communication and PSHE, and also in the core areas of Literacy, Numeracy and ICT. We work hard to make sure that learning for our pupils is relevant, functional and fun and use all resources available to us, both in terms of our school facilities and the local community around us. We work together as a department to ensure that all pupils' learning needs are met, which may involve integration of individual pupils in specific sessions with another class.
To provide breadth to our curriculum we follow the school's four-yearly topic cycle and learn about all sorts of interesting things. Within these topics we look for opportunities to work together as a department, holding events such as our 'Stories performance', Chinese New Year celebration and 'Water Extravaganza'! We have regular residential trips to Hindleap Warren and have also enjoyed camps on the school field. We are also keen to involve parents in their children's learning and often hold events for parents to attend, as well as having regular opportunities to update them on their children's progress and discuss next steps.

The school website is designed to be parent friendly and is full of information about the school, including whole school pupil achievement and OFSTED reports. Prospective parents, grandparents, and friends are encouraged to look at the website.
